newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks make steady 1.7 pct climb in week.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks make steady 1.7 pct climb in week.

text.p: Cyprus equities closed the week 1.7 percent higher on Friday in a rebound countering depressed trading of last month.
The 43-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index closed the week at 76.48 points, up from 75.22 points recorded last week.

"Technical analysis this week points to a short-term bullish market as the nine-day moving average reversed last week's downward trend," said CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation, a member of the Bank of Cyprus Group .
All but one of the seven sub indices rose. The banking sector saw gains of 1.86 percent, and the approved investment index rose 1.96 percent.
Bank of Cyprus shares were trading at 299.5 on Friday, up 4.5 cents from last week, while Bank of Cyprus nil paid rights shares, which made their debut on June 2, were trading at 99.5, up five cents.
CISCO said Bank of Cyprus nil-paid rights contributed significantly to the rise of the market on high investor demand.
The Cyprus Popular Bank closing price was 306.5 on Friday, jumping eight cents from last week.
The Hellenic Bank gained one cent, closing at 280.5 and Universal Savings Bank was trading at 181 cents, the same as last week.
Universal Life Insurance was up 5.5 cents to 466 while Interamerican Insurance dropped one cent to 92.5. Paneuropean shares were trading at 101.5 from 101 last week.
Blue-chip cement manufacturers Vassiliko were up 2.5 cents at 159 and Cyprus Cement retreated half a cent to 249.
Shares of beer and wine company KEO were trading at 102 from 103.5 last week.
